I'm 73 this year, been farming these same fields for 50 years since I was a young man. Only went to primary school, but I know my land better than any book. I've got 13.1 mu here in Quzhou — not big, not small. About 9 mu I do wheat and then maize right after, and the other 4.1 mu I plant cotton. Six people in the house, but the young ones work in the city and send some money back. It's mostly me, my old woman, and my daughter-in-law doing the farm work now. My legs and back aren't what they used to be, so I have to hire help for the heavy times.

Well, it's late April now. My wheat went in last October, around the 10th, same as always. I used my own saved seed — that red-grain variety my nephew gave me a few years back, does well in this soil. I already put the base fertilizer down before planting, about 10 kg of urea and some phosphate per mu, and then topdressed another 8 kg of urea at jointing time back in March. The wheat looks okay this year, not great but okay. I'll irrigate one more time when the grain is filling, probably mid-May. For harvest in early June I'll hire one or two people from the village to help with the cutting. That costs me but I can't swing a scythe like I used to.

The cotton — I'm planting it right now, this very week. Got about 4.1 mu of it. I saved my own cotton seed from last year, don't buy new every time, too expensive. I put about 7 kg of fertilizer per mu in the furrow when I plant, and later I'll side-dress another 5 kg when it starts flowering. Cotton needs a lot of hand work, especially picking. My daughter-in-law will help but I'll need to hire village women for the picking, probably 10 days of hired labor all told. That's about 800 yuan right there, but what can you do? The body doesn't bend like it used to. Last year I got about 220 kg per mu of seed cotton, hoping for the same if the bolls set well.

For the maize, that goes in right after wheat comes off in early June. I plant fast — usually within two or three days of cutting wheat, no time to waste in this double-crop system. I'll buy hybrid seed, about 50 yuan per mu. Put 10 kg of urea at planting and another 8 kg when the leaves get big and the stalk is tall. Irrigate twice if it's dry, which it usually is. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

Money is always tight. All together I'm looking at about 5,900 yuan in input costs this year. The kids send some back from town but I still lose sleep over it. I thought about putting more fertilizer on the wheat, but fertilizer got expensive and I can't risk having no cash left if a drought hits or prices drop. Better to do what I know works. My neighbor tried some new fertilizer last year and it didn't do any better than mine, so I'll stick to my way.
